verdict: Ads are generating sales but at a loss — spend outpaces return this period.
diagnosis: Instagram ads spent $5,776 and returned $28,675 in tracked purchases, but cost per purchase sits near $182 — unsustainable for most meat baskets.

signals.headline: Cost per purchase hit $182
signals.detail: Each sale cost roughly $182 in ad spend this period. Average order value needs to clear that comfortably to make money.

signals.headline: 649 purchases from $5,776 spend
signals.detail: Volume is real, but the math only works if repeat orders follow. First-order economics look thin.

signals.headline: 658 add-to-carts, 228 checkouts
signals.detail: About one in three carts started checkout. Cart-to-checkout drop-off is the single biggest leak this period.

signals.headline: 273 reviews added, 5-star average
signals.detail: Reputation is strong and growing. This is an underused asset in ads and on product pages right now.

signals.headline: Followers grew by 210
signals.detail: Organic Instagram growth is slow given ad volume. Content is not converting viewers into followers at scale.

recommendations.title: Fix the checkout drop-off before scaling spend
recommendations.detail: Only 228 of 658 add-to-carts reached checkout. Test guest checkout, shipping cost transparency upfront, and a simpler mobile flow before adding budget.

recommendations.title: Test a bundle or threshold to lift order value
recommendations.detail: At $182 cost per purchase, average order value must clear that. Consider a free-shipping threshold or starter bundle aimed at $150+ baskets.

recommendations.title: Put the 273 reviews to work in ads
recommendations.detail: Reputation is a strength. Test review-led image and video creative against the current Premium Cuts image to lower cost per purchase.
